ai.description: This gecko reaches 8 cm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal crossbands and a pale nuchal collar. Distinctive features include strongly curved toes and a granular, non-tuberculate dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus gubernatoris* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped or chevron-like nuchal marking on the nape, absent in most similar species.
ai.habitat: The Sikkimese Bent-toed Gecko inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests in the Himalayan foothills, typically found at elevations between 300 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sikkimese bent-toed gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates on rock faces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus gubernatoris* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sikkimese Bent-toed Gecko is endemic to the Himalayan foothills in the Indian state of Sikkim, typically inhabiting elevations between 300 and 1,500 meters.
